title.raw: 卷68 甄琛 高聰 Volume 68: Zhen Chen, Gao Cong

sentences.zh: 甄琛 高聰

translations.literal: Zhen Chen; Gao Cong
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen and Gao Cong

sentences.zh: 甄琛，字思伯，中山毋極人，漢太保甄邯後也。

translations.literal: Zhen Chen, style name Sibo, a man of Wuji in Zhongshan, a descendant of Zhen Han, Grand Protector of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen, courtesy name Sibo, was a native of Wuji in Zhongshan and traced his line to Zhen Han, Grand Protector of the Han.

sentences.zh: 父凝，州主簿。

translations.literal: His father Ning was a prefectural chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Ning, served as chief clerk of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 琛少敏悟，閨門之內，兄弟戲狎，不以禮法自居。

translations.literal: From youth Chen was quick and perceptive; within the inner quarters he and his brothers jested familiarly and did not hold themselves to ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was clever from boyhood. At home he and his brothers fooled around without observing formal propriety.

sentences.zh: 頗學經史，稱有刀筆，而形貌短陋，尠風儀。

translations.literal: He studied the classics and histories considerably and was said to have skill with the written brush, but his form was short and ugly and he had little bearing and grace.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and had a reputation for literary skill, but he was short, homely, and lacking in presence.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才。

translations.literal: He was nominated as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a Cultivated Talent.

sentences.zh: 入都積歲，頗以弈棊棄日，至乃通夜不止。

translations.literal: After entering the capital he accumulated years, largely casting away days in board games, even to the point of not stopping through whole nights.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital he lingered for years, frittering away his days at chess and often playing straight through the night.

sentences.zh: 手下蒼頭常令秉燭，或時睡頓，大加其杖，如此非一。

translations.literal: The blue-clad servants under him he would often order to hold candles; if they sometimes nodded off, he would greatly increase their beating—this was not once only.
translations.idiomatic: He habitually made his house servants hold candles while he played; if they dozed off he would thrash them severely, and this happened again and again.

sentences.zh: 奴後不勝楚痛，乃白琛曰：「郎君辭父母，仕宦京師，若為讀書執燭，奴不敢辭罪，乃以圍棊，日夜不息，豈是向京之意？

translations.literal: The slave afterward could not bear the pain of the flogging and thus reported to Chen, saying: "Young master, having left your parents to take office in the capital—if it were to hold candles for reading, this slave would not dare refuse punishment; yet you use go day and night without cease—is this your intent in coming to the capital?
translations.idiomatic: Finally one servant, unable to endure the lashings, spoke up: "Sir, you left your family to take a post in the capital. I would accept a beating without complaint if you kept me up to study—but you spend every waking hour at the board. Is that why you came to the capital?

sentences.zh: 而賜加杖罰，不亦非理！

translations.literal: Yet you bestow added stick punishment—is that not also against reason!
translations.idiomatic: And then you beat us for it—is that not unjust as well?

sentences.zh: 」琛惕然慚感，遂從許叡、李彪假書研習，聞見益優。

translations.literal: " Chen was startled, ashamed, and moved; he then from Xu Rui and Li Biao borrowed books to study and investigate, and his hearing and seeing steadily became superior.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was shaken and ashamed. He borrowed books from Xu Rui and Li Biao and applied himself to study; his learning steadily deepened.

sentences.zh: 太和初，拜中書博士，遷諫議大夫，時有所陳，亦為高祖知賞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign he was appointed Master of Writing in the Secretariat, was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, and at times made memorials, which Emperor Xiaowen also knew and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taihe era he was made a Secretariat academician, then promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master. His memorials won notice and favor from Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎侍郎，出為本州征北府長史，後為本州陽平王頤衞軍府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Direct-and-Upright Palatial Cavalry, went out as chief clerk of the Northern Campaigning Headquarters of his home province, and afterward was chief clerk of the Guard Army headquarters of Prince Yangping of his home province, Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Direct-and-Upright Gentleman of the Palatial Cavalry, then left the capital to serve as chief clerk on his province's Northern Campaign headquarters staff and later on the staff of Prince Yangping Yuan Yi's guard headquarters in the same province.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐祚，以琛為中散大夫、兼御史中尉，轉通直散騎常侍，仍兼中尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Chen was made Grand Master of the Palace Rescript and concurrently Censor Commandant, was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Direct-and-Upright Palatial Cavalry, and still concurrently held Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne, Chen was appointed Palace Rescript Grand Master and concurrent Censor Commandant, then promoted to Regular Attendant of the Palatial Cavalry while retaining the censor post.

sentences.zh: 琛表曰：

translations.literal: Chen memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 王者道同天壤，施齊造化，濟時拯物，為民父母。

translations.literal: The way of the king is the same as heaven and earth; his bestowal equals creation and transformation; he succors the age and saves things, acting as father and mother to the people.
translations.idiomatic: A true ruler's path aligns with heaven and earth; his bounty matches creation itself. He rescues the age and redeems the living, standing as father and mother to the people.

sentences.zh: 故年穀不登，為民祈祀。

translations.literal: Therefore when the year's grain does not rise, he performs sacrifice and prayer for the people.
translations.idiomatic: When harvests fail, he performs rites on the people's behalf.

sentences.zh: 乾坤所惠，天子順之；

translations.literal: What heaven and earth bestow, the Son of Heaven follows it;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever heaven and earth provide, the Son of Heaven accepts in turn;

sentences.zh: 山川祕利，天子通之。

translations.literal: the secret profits of mountains and rivers, the Son of Heaven opens them.
translations.idiomatic: whatever wealth lies hidden in mountains and rivers, the Son of Heaven opens it to use.

sentences.zh: 苟益生民，損躬無吝，如或所聚，唯為賑恤。

translations.literal: If it profits the living people, he is not grudging to diminish his person; if there is gathering, it is solely for relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: If the people may benefit, he does not hesitate to spend himself; whatever is gathered serves only relief.

sentences.zh: 是以月令稱：山林藪澤，有能取蔬食禽獸者，皆野虞教導之；

translations.literal: Therefore the Monthly Ordinances say: in forests, marshes, and wetlands, those able to take vegetables, food, birds, and beasts—all are instructed and guided by the wildland overseers;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Monthly Ordinances state that in forests, marshes, and wetlands, gatherers of plants and hunters of game are all to be guided by wildland overseers.

sentences.zh: 其迭相侵奪者，罪之無赦。

translations.literal: those who successively encroach and seize upon one another—to them punishment without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual encroachment and seizure are crimes punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 此明導民而弗禁，通有無以相濟也。

translations.literal: This makes clear guiding the people rather than forbidding them—opening presence and absence to aid one another.
translations.idiomatic: This shows the principle of guiding the people rather than forbidding them—allowing plenty and want to balance one another.

sentences.zh: 周禮雖有川澤之禁，正所以防其殘盡，必令取之有時。

translations.literal: Although the Rites of Zhou have prohibitions on rivers and marshes, this is precisely to guard against their being exhausted and used up, necessarily requiring that taking have its seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou do impose restrictions on rivers and marshes, but only to prevent exhaustion—gathering must follow seasons.

sentences.zh: 斯所謂鄣護雖在公，更所以為民守之耳。

translations.literal: This is what is called: although the barrier protection rests with the public authority, all the more it is for guarding on behalf of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Protection may rest with the state, but its purpose is to safeguard resources for the people.

sentences.zh: 且一家之長，惠及子孫，一運之君，澤周天下，皆所以厚其所養，以為國家之富。

translations.literal: Moreover a head of one family extends benefit to sons and grandsons; a ruler of one age extends favor throughout the realm—all to enrich what they nourish as the wealth of the state.
translations.idiomatic: As a family head enriches his descendants, so a dynastic ruler spreads bounty across the realm—thickening what he sustains to build the state's wealth.

sentences.zh: 未有尊居父母，而醯醢是吝；

translations.literal: There is never one who honors and dwells as parent yet is grudging of pickles and sauces;
translations.idiomatic: No one who holds parental authority hoards condiments from his household;

sentences.zh: 富有萬品，而一物是規。

translations.literal: possessing the myriad goods yet regarding one thing only.
translations.idiomatic: nor does a man rich in every commodity cling to a single item.

sentences.zh: 今者，天為黔首生鹽，國與黔首鄣護，假獲其利，是猶富專口齗不及四體也。

translations.literal: Now heaven has produced salt for the black-headed people; the state with the black-headed people barrier-protects it and they falsely obtain its profit—this is like being wealthy yet dedicating the mouth's gums and not reaching the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave salt to the common people, yet the state fences it off with them and claims the profit—like a rich man who feeds only his gums while starving his limbs.

sentences.zh: 且天下夫婦歲貢粟帛。

translations.literal: Moreover every couple in the realm yearly presents grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Every household in the empire pays grain and silk each year.

sentences.zh: 四海之有，備奉一人；

translations.literal: What the four seas possesses—all is prepared to serve one man;
translations.idiomatic: All that the four seas hold serves a single man;

sentences.zh: 軍國之資，取給百姓。

translations.literal: the resources of army and state are taken and supplied from the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: the armies and the state draw their sustenance from the people.

sentences.zh: 天子亦何患乎貧，而苟禁一池也。

translations.literal: What need has the Son of Heaven to worry about poverty, yet begrudgingly forbid one salt pond?
translations.idiomatic: Why should the Son of Heaven fear poverty—and yet hoard a single salt pool?

sentences.zh: 古之王者，世有其民，[1]或水火以濟其用，或巢宇以誨其居，或教農以去其飢，或訓衣以除其弊。

translations.literal: The ancient kings, age after age had their people, [1] some with fire and water to aid their use, some with nests and dwellings to teach their abodes, some teaching agriculture to remove their hunger, some instructing clothing to remove their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Kings of old each had their own people: some brought fire and water to serve daily needs, some taught them to build shelters, some taught farming to end hunger, some taught cloth-making to end nakedness.

sentences.zh: 故周詩稱「教之誨之，飲之食之」，皆所以撫覆導養，為之求利者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Zhou odes say "teach them, instruct them, give them drink, give them food"—all to soothe, cover, guide, and nourish, and for them seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes sings, "Teach them, guide them, feed them, give them drink"—all acts of sheltering, guiding, and nurturing, seeking the people's good.

sentences.zh: 臣性昧知理，識無遠尚，每觀上古愛民之迹，時讀中葉驟稅之書，未嘗不歎彼遠大，惜此近狹。

translations.literal: This subject by nature is dull in knowing principle, without far-reaching views; whenever I observe the traces of ancient times in loving the people, and at times read the books of middle ages on sudden taxation, I have never not sighed at their vast reach and grieved at this narrow nearness.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of limited vision. Whenever I read how the ancients loved their people and then turn to the tax records of recent dynasties, I cannot help sighing at their generosity and grieving at our meanness.

sentences.zh: 今偽弊相承，仍崇關鄽之稅；

translations.literal: Now false troubles succeed one another and still honor market-pass and shop taxes;
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt regimes pile policy upon policy, still levying heavy market duties;

sentences.zh: 大魏恢博，唯受穀帛之輸。

translations.literal: Great Wei is vast and broad and only receives the grain-and-silk tribute.
translations.idiomatic: yet great Wei is magnanimous and accepts only grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 是使遠方聞者，罔不歌德。

translations.literal: this causes those afar who hear of it—all without exception to sing its virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Those far away who hear of it cannot help praising its virtue.

sentences.zh: 昔亶父以棄寶得民，碩鼠以受財失眾。

translations.literal: In former times Duke Danfu by abandoning treasure gained the people; the large rat by receiving wealth lost the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Danfu once won the people by giving up treasure; the "fat rat" ode warns that greed costs the multitude.

sentences.zh: 君王之義，宜其高矣；

translations.literal: the kingly principle—how high it should be!
translations.idiomatic: The measure of kingship should be lofty;

sentences.zh: 魏之簡稅，惠實遠矣。

translations.literal: Wei's simplified taxes—its kindness truly reaches far.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's light levies show a kindness that reaches far indeed.

sentences.zh: 語稱出內之吝，有司之福；

translations.literal: The saying states: stinginess in disbursement from the inner treasury is the blessing of the clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Proverbs say that stinginess in expenditure blesses clerks

sentences.zh: 施惠之難，人君之禍。

translations.literal: the difficulty of bestowing kindness is the misfortune of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: while difficulty in granting favors becomes the ruler's curse.

sentences.zh: 夫以府藏之物，猶以不施而為災，況府外之利，而可吝之於黔首？

translations.literal: How much more with goods in the treasury—even not bestowing them becomes disaster; how much more profits outside the treasury—how can they be grudged to the black-headed people?
translations.idiomatic: Even stored treasure brings disaster if withheld—how much more wealth lying outside the treasury! How can it be denied to the people?

sentences.zh: 且善藏者藏於民，不善藏者藏於府。

translations.literal: Moreover those good at storing store in the people; those not good at storing store in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Wise hoarding fills the people; foolish hoarding fills the treasury.

sentences.zh: 藏於民者民欣而君富，藏於府者國怨而民貧。

translations.literal: stored in the people—the people rejoice and the ruler is rich; stored in the treasury—the state resents and the people are poor.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth among the people brings joy to them and riches to the ruler; wealth locked in the treasury breeds resentment in the state and poverty among the people.

sentences.zh: 國怨則示化有虧，民貧則君無所取。

translations.literal: When the state resents, it shows the transforming influence has fallen short; when the people are poor, the ruler has nowhere from which to take.
translations.idiomatic: A resentful state means deficient governance; a poor people means the ruler has nothing to draw upon.

sentences.zh: 願弛茲鹽禁，使沛然遠及，依周禮置川衡之法，使之監導而已。

translations.literal: I wish to relax this salt prohibition, making it flood broadly and reach afar; following the Zhou Rites to establish the law of river overseers, having them only oversee and guide.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this salt monopoly be relaxed and its benefits allowed to flow far and wide; following the Zhou model, appoint river overseers to supervise and guide the trade—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「民利在斯，深如所陳。

translations.literal: The edict stated: "The people's profit lies herein; profound as what was memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The people's welfare is at stake here, and your argument is weighty.

sentences.zh: 付八座議可否以聞。」

translations.literal: Hand it to the Eight Seats to deliberate whether it may be implemented and report."
translations.idiomatic: Send this to the Eight Ministers for debate and report their decision."

sentences.zh: 司徒、錄尚書、彭城王勰，兼尚書邢巒等奏：「琛之所列，富乎有言，首尾大備，或無可貶。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masses, Recorder of the Secretariat, Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, and Concurrent Secretariat Minister Xing Luan and others memorialized: "What Chen has set forth is richer than having words; beginning and end greatly complete—perhaps nothing to censure.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Masses, Secretariat Director, Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, and Concurrent Minister Xing Luan submitted a joint memorial: "Chen's argument is eloquent and thorough from start to finish—there may be little to fault.

sentences.zh: 但恐坐談則理高，行之則事闕，是用遲回，未謂為可。

translations.literal: But I fear sitting and talking then principle is lofty, yet carrying it out then affairs fall short; therefore I hesitate and turn back and do not deem it feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that in discussion his reasoning sounds lofty while in practice it would fall short. For that reason we hesitate and do not consider it workable.

sentences.zh: 竊惟古之善為治者，莫不昭其勝途，悟其遠理，及於救世，升降稱時。

translations.literal: I secretly consider that among the ancients good at governing, none failed to make clear their victorious paths, awaken to their far-reaching principles, and when it came to saving the age, rise and fall according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the ancients who governed well all illuminated the path to success, grasped principles that reached far ahead, and when saving the age adjusted their policies to suit the times.

sentences.zh: 欲令豐無過溢，儉不致弊，役養消息，備在厥中，節約取足，成其性命。

translations.literal: They wished to make abundance not pass into overflow, frugality not reach to ruin, labor and nurture waxing and waning—all complete within this, economizing to take sufficiency and completing their lives and natures.
translations.idiomatic: They sought abundance without excess, thrift without ruin, and balanced labor with nurture so that restraint yielded sufficiency and the people could live out their lives.

sentences.zh: 如不爾者，焉用君為？

translations.literal: If it were not thus, of what use is having a ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, what need is there for a ruler?

sentences.zh: 若任其生產，隨其啄食，便是芻狗萬物，不相有矣。

translations.literal: If one let them produce as they will and follow their pecking and eating, this would be straw dogs for the myriad things—not possessing one another.
translations.idiomatic: To let everyone produce at will and take what they peck at would reduce all things to straw dogs with no mutual obligation.

sentences.zh: 自大道既往，恩惠生焉，下奉上施，卑高理睦。

translations.literal: Since the Great Way has passed away, favor and grace were born; below offering up, above bestowing down—the low and high in principle harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Great Way receded, structured favor arose: the lower ranks offered tribute upward and the higher bestowed gifts downward, harmonizing high and low.

sentences.zh: 然恩惠既交，思拯之術廣，恒恐財不賙國，澤不厚民。

translations.literal: Yet once favor and grace had been exchanged, thoughts of methods to rescue broadened, constantly fearing wealth would not suffice for the state and bounty would not enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once such exchange was established, rulers sought ever broader means of relief, always fearing that revenue would not sustain the state or bounty reach the people.

sentences.zh: 故多方以達其情，立法以行其志。

translations.literal: Therefore by many means to reach their sentiments, by establishing laws to carry out their aims.
translations.idiomatic: Hence they devised many channels to understand the people's needs and enacted laws to carry out their intent.

sentences.zh: 至乃取貨山川，輕在民之貢；

translations.literal: even to taking goods from mountains and rivers, lightening what lay on the people's tribute;
translations.idiomatic: They even drew revenue from mountains and rivers while lightening the people's direct tribute;

sentences.zh: 立稅關市，裨十一之儲。

translations.literal: established taxes at passes and markets, to aid the one-tenth storage.
translations.idiomatic: imposed duties at passes and markets to supplement the tithe stored for the state.

sentences.zh: 收此與彼，非利己也；

translations.literal: gathering this and giving that—not for self-profit;
translations.idiomatic: taking here to give there—not for private gain;

sentences.zh: 回彼就此，非為身也。

translations.literal: turning that back to reach this—not for the person.
translations.idiomatic: redirecting resources—not for personal enrichment.

sentences.zh: 所謂集天地之產，惠天地之民，藉造物之富，賑造物之貧。

translations.literal: This is what is called gathering the productions of heaven and earth, bestowing favor on the people of heaven and earth, borrowing the wealth of the Creator, and relieving the poverty of the Created.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to gather heaven and earth's bounty, shower it on heaven and earth's people, borrow creation's wealth, and relieve creation's poor.

sentences.zh: 徹商賈給戎戰，賦四民贍軍國，取乎用乎，各有義已。

translations.literal: levying merchants to supply military campaigns, assessing the four peoples to support army and state—taking and using, each had its righteousness complete.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants were taxed to fund campaigns; the four classes were assessed to sustain army and state—each levy had its proper purpose in use.

sentences.zh: 禁此淵池，不專大官之御；

translations.literal: forbidding this deep pool—not solely for the great officers' provisions;
translations.idiomatic: restricting this salt pool was not to stock the grand officers' kitchens alone;

sentences.zh: 斂此匹帛，豈為後宮之資。

translations.literal: collecting this bolt of silk—how could it be for the rear palace's resources?
translations.idiomatic: collecting each bolt of silk—surely not merely to fill the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 既潤不在己，彼我理一，猶積而散之，將焉所吝？

translations.literal: Since enrichment does not rest in oneself, other and self in principle are one—still accumulating yet dispersing it; where would there be grudging?
translations.idiomatic: Since the benefit does not stay with the collector, self and other share one logic—wealth is gathered only to be dispersed. What is there to begrudge?

sentences.zh: 且稅之本意，事有可求，固以希濟生民，非為富賄藏貨。

translations.literal: Moreover the root meaning of taxation—in affairs there is what may be sought; solidly thereby hoping to succor the living people, not to enrich bribes and hoard goods.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the root purpose of taxation is achievable: to aid the living people, not to amass bribes and hoard treasure.

sentences.zh: 不爾者，昔之君子何為然哉？

translations.literal: If it were not thus, why did the gentlemen of old act so?
translations.idiomatic: If not, why did the gentlemen of old do likewise?

sentences.zh: 是以後來經圖，未之或改。

translations.literal: Therefore later generations in their canonical plans never altered it.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties therefore left these institutions unchanged.

sentences.zh: 故先朝商校，小大以情，降鑒之流，疑興復鹽禁。

translations.literal: Therefore the former court deliberated and compared, great and small according to sentiment; the stream of lowered mirrors suspected reviving the salt prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Our former court weighed the matter carefully, great and small according to circumstance, and imperial reflection inclined toward restoring the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 然自行以來，典司多怠，出入之間，事不如法，遂令細民怨嗟，商販輕議，此乃用之者無方，非興之者有謬。

translations.literal: Yet from the time of implementation the overseers were mostly slack; in comings and goings affairs did not accord with law, thus causing common people to lament and merchants lightly to criticize—this is that those who applied it lacked method, not that those who established it were in error.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since implementation the overseers have been negligent and transactions have not followed the law, provoking popular complaint and merchant gossip. The fault lies with those who administer the system, not with those who established it.

sentences.zh: 至使朝廷明識，聽瑩其間，今而罷之，懼失前旨。

translations.literal: To the point that the court's clear understanding listened brightly within it; now to abolish it—I fear losing the former intent.
translations.idiomatic: The court's clear judgment has weighed this carefully; to abolish the system now would risk abandoning our former intent.

sentences.zh: 一行一改，法若易棊，參論理要，宜依前式。

translations.literal: One enactment one change—law as if changing go pieces; jointly discussing principle's essentials, it is fitting to follow the former model.
translations.idiomatic: Law changed with every new measure would be like shifting pieces on a board. On balance, the prior system should stand.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「司鹽之稅，乃自古通典，然興制利民，亦代或不同，苟可以富氓益化，唯理所在。

translations.literal: " The edict stated: "The salt-administration tax is an ancient universal statute; yet establishing institutions to benefit the people also differs age by age—if it can enrich the common folk and increase transformation, only where principle lies.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict replied: "The salt tax is an ancient institution, yet each age frames policy to benefit the people differently. Wherever the people may be enriched and civilization advanced, that is where principle lies.

sentences.zh: 甄琛之表，實所謂助政毗治者也，可從其前計，使公私並宜，川利無擁。

translations.literal: Zhen Chen's memorial is truly what is called aiding governance and assisting rule; his former plan may be followed, making public and private alike fitting and river profits without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen's memorial truly aids governance. Follow his earlier proposal so that public and private interests are balanced and river commerce flows unblocked.

sentences.zh: 尚書嚴為禁豪強之制也。」

translations.literal: Let the Secretariat strictly enact regulations forbidding powerful clans."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Secretariat strictly enforce measures against powerful predators."

sentences.zh: 詔琛參八座議事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chen to participate in the Eight Seats' deliberations on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was ordered to join the Eight Ministers in policy deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尋正中尉，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made Regular Censor Commandant, Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Regular Censor Commandant while retaining his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，領中尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and headed the Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and continued to head the censorate.

sentences.zh: 琛俛眉畏避，不能繩糾貴遊，凡所劾治，率多下吏。

translations.literal: Chen lowered his brows in fear and avoidance, unable to bind and correct the noble wanderers; whatever he impeached and tried mostly went down to subordinate clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Chen bowed his head in fear and could not rein in the privileged wanderers; cases he pursued usually ended with low-ranking clerks punished instead.

sentences.zh: 於時趙脩盛寵，琛傾身事之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Xiu enjoyed overflowing favor; Chen bent his person to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Xiu enjoyed extravagant favor, and Chen threw himself into serving him.

sentences.zh: 琛父凝為中散大夫，弟僧林為本州別駕，皆託脩申達。

translations.literal: Chen's father Ning was Grand Master of the Palace Rescript; his younger brother Senglin was Vice-Prefect of his home province—all entrusted Xiu to convey and reach upward.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's father Ning was a Palace Rescript Grand Master and his younger brother Senglin was vice-prefect of their home province; both relied on Xiu to advance their interests at court.

sentences.zh: 至脩姦詐事露，明當收考，今日乃舉其罪。

translations.literal: When Xiu's treacherous and deceitful affairs were exposed and it was clear he should be seized and examined, only on that day did Chen raise his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu's fraud was exposed and arrest was clearly due, Chen reported his crimes only that day.

sentences.zh: 及監決脩鞭，猶相隱惻，然告人曰：「趙脩小人，背如土牛，殊耐鞭杖。

translations.literal: When overseeing the execution of flogging Xiu, he still mutually concealed sympathy, yet told others: "Zhao Xiu is a petty man; his back is like an earthen ox and especially endures the whip and staff.
translations.idiomatic: When supervising Xiu's flogging he still showed sympathy, yet told others, "Zhao Xiu is a petty fellow—his back is like an earthen ox and takes the lash remarkably well.

sentences.zh: 」有識以此非之。

translations.literal: " Men of discernment for this censured him.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of judgment condemned him for this.

sentences.zh: 脩死之明日，琛與黃門郎李憑以朋黨被召詣尚書，兼尚書元英、邢巒窮其阿附之狀。

translations.literal: On the day after Xiu's death, Chen and Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Ping were summoned to the Secretariat on account of faction, and Concurrent Ministers Yuan Ying and Xing Luan thoroughly investigated their fawning attachment.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Xiu died, Chen and Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Ping were summoned to the Secretariat on faction charges; Concurrent Ministers Yuan Ying and Xing Luan exhaustively investigated their collusion.

sentences.zh: 琛曾拜官，諸賓悉集，巒乃晚至，琛謂巒曰：「卿何處放蛆來，今晚始顧？

translations.literal: Chen had once received an appointment and all guests were gathered; Luan then arrived late. Chen said to Luan: "Where did you release maggots that you only turn your gaze tonight?
translations.idiomatic: Chen had once held a reception and all guests had gathered when Luan arrived late. Chen said to him, "Where did you breed your maggots that you only show up tonight?

sentences.zh: 」雖以戲言，巒變色銜忿，及此，大相推窮。

translations.literal: " Although it was jesting words, Luan changed color and harbored resentment; reaching this point, they greatly pressed and exhausted one another.
translations.idiomatic: " Though meant as a joke, Luan flushed with resentment; when the investigation came, he pressed the case relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 司徒公、錄尚書、北海王詳等奏曰：「臣聞黨人為患，自古所疾；

translations.literal: Duke of the Masses, Recorder of the Secretariat, Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang and others memorialized, saying: "Your subject has heard that factionalists as a calamity have been detested since antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Masses, Secretariat Director, Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang, and others memorialized: "We have heard that factionalism has been a scourge since antiquity;

sentences.zh: 政之所忌，雖寵必誅，皆所以存天下之至公，保靈基於永業者也。

translations.literal: what government most dreads—even if favored, must be punished—all to preserve the utmost fairness under heaven and secure the numinous foundation in everlasting enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: what government most dreads—even favorites must be punished—all to preserve the empire's utmost fairness and secure the dynasty's foundation for ages.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下纂聖前暉，淵鑒幽慝，恩斷近習，憲軌唯新，大政蔚以增光，鴻猷於焉永泰。

translations.literal: Bowingly considering that Your Majesty inherits the sage's former radiance, profoundly mirrors hidden wickedness, with grace severing close favorites and penal statutes solely renewed—great governance flourishes and increases in glory; the vast plan thereby is ever secure.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the sage-kings' radiance, discerns hidden wickedness, cuts off favoritism toward intimates, and renews the penal code—great governance flourishes and the grand design endures in security.

sentences.zh: 謹案：侍中、領御史中尉甄琛，身居直法，糾摘是司，風邪響黷，猶宜劾糾，況趙脩奢暴，聲著內外，侵公害私，朝野切齒。

translations.literal: Carefully investigating: Palace Attendant and Head Censor Commandant Zhen Chen, his person occupying upright law and impeachment his charge—even wind perversity and echo corruption should still be impeached; how much more Zhao Xiu's extravagance and violence, fame resounding inside and outside, encroaching on the public to benefit the private—the court and wildlands gnash teeth.
translations.idiomatic: We find that Palace Attendant and Censor Commandant Zhen Chen holds the office of upright law and impeachment—he should have prosecuted even minor corruption, let alone Zhao Xiu's extravagance and violence, notorious inside and outside the court, plundering the public for private gain until all gnashed their teeth.

sentences.zh: 而琛嘗不陳奏，方更往來，綢繆結納，以為朋黨，中外影響，致其談譽。

translations.literal: Yet Chen never once memorialized; instead he further came and went, closely binding and joining as a faction, inside and outside echoing in influence, bringing about his talk and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chen never reported him; instead he kept company with him, forming close ties as a faction, swaying opinion inside and outside court until praise spread.

sentences.zh: 令布衣之父，超登正四之官；

translations.literal: He caused a father in plain cloth to leap and ascend to a regular fourth-rank post;
translations.idiomatic: He secured for his commoner father a leap to a regular fourth-rank post;

sentences.zh: 七品之弟，越陟三階之祿。

translations.literal: a seventh-rank younger brother to cross and ascend three grades of salary.
translations.idiomatic: and for his seventh-rank younger brother a promotion across three salary grades.

sentences.zh: 虧先皇之選典，塵聖明之官人。

translations.literal: This falls short of the former emperor's selection canon and soils the sage-bright officeholders.
translations.idiomatic: This violated the late emperor's standards of selection and stained Your Majesty's roster of officials.

sentences.zh: 又與武衞將軍、黃門郎李憑相為表裏，憑兄叨封，知而不言。

translations.literal: Moreover with Martial Guard General and Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Ping he was mutually outer and inner; Ping's elder brother presumptuously received enfeoffment—knowing yet not speaking.
translations.idiomatic: He also acted in concert with Martial Guard General and Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Ping; when Ping's elder brother received an improper enfeoffment, Chen knew but said nothing.

sentences.zh: 及脩釁彰，方加彈奏。

translations.literal: Only when Xiu's offense became manifest did he then add impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Xiu's crimes were exposed did he lodge impeachment.

sentences.zh: 生則附其形勢，死則就地排之，竊天之功以為己力，仰欺朝廷，俯罔百司，其為鄙詐，於茲甚矣。

translations.literal: While alive he attached to his power and position; when dead he pushed him down on the spot, stealing heaven's achievement to make it his own strength, looking up to deceive the court, looking down to deceive the hundred offices—his baseness and deceit, at this point, were extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In life he had clung to Xiu's power; in death he cast him down. He stole credit due heaven for his own gain, deceiving the throne above and the bureaucracy below. His baseness and fraud could scarcely go further.

sentences.zh: 不實不忠，實合貶黜。

translations.literal: Untruthful and disloyal—truly fitting demotion and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Dishonest and disloyal, he deserved demotion and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 謹依律科徒，請以職除。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to law, sentence to penal labor; request removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully apply the statute sentencing him to penal servitude and request his dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 其父中散，實為叨越，雖皇族帝孫，未有此例，既得不以倫，請下收奪。

translations.literal: His father's Grand Master of the Palace Rescript post was truly overreaching; though royal-house imperial grandsons have no such precedent—having obtained it against proper order, request stripping and seizure below.
translations.idiomatic: His father's post as Palace Rescript Grand Master was a clear overreach; even for imperial clansmen of the royal house no such precedent exists. Since the appointment violated proper order, we request that it be revoked.

sentences.zh: 李憑朋附趙脩，是親是仗，交遊之道，不依恒度，或晨昏從就，或吉凶往來，至乃身拜其親，妻見其子，每有家事，必先請託。

translations.literal: Li Ping factionally attached to Zhao Xiu, making him kin and relying on him; the way of social exchange did not follow constant measure—sometimes attending from dawn to dusk, sometimes coming and going for luck or misfortune, even to bowing in person to Xiu's kin while his wife received Xiu's son; whenever there was household business, he would first request and entrust.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping attached himself to Zhao Xiu as kin and patron. His social dealings ignored all bounds: he might attend from dawn to dusk or visit for every joy or sorrow, even bowing in person to Xiu's relatives while his wife received Xiu's son. For any household matter he sought Xiu's patronage first.

sentences.zh: 緇點皇風，塵鄙正化。

translations.literal: Blackening and staining the imperial wind, dusting and defiling orthodox transformation.
translations.idiomatic: They stained the imperial ethos and defiled orthodox governance.

sentences.zh: 此而不糾，將何以肅整阿諛，奬厲忠概！

translations.literal: If this is not impeached, by what means will one rectify flattery and exhort loyal integrity!
translations.idiomatic: If such conduct goes unprosecuted, how will flattery be disciplined or loyal integrity be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 請免所居官，以肅風軌。

translations.literal: Request removal from his occupied offices to rectify the wind and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that he be removed from office to restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 琛遂免歸本郡，左右相連死黜者三十餘人。

translations.literal: Chen was then dismissed and returned to his home commandery; more than thirty of his close associates were linked, executed, or dismissed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was dismissed and sent home to his commandery; more than thirty of his close associates were executed or dismissed in the fallout.

sentences.zh: 始，琛以父母年老，常求解官扶侍，故高祖授以本州長史。

translations.literal: At first, because Chen's parents were old he had often requested release from office to support them, so Emperor Xiaowen appointed him chief administrator of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because his parents were elderly, Chen had often asked to leave office to care for them, and Emperor Xiaowen appointed him chief administrator of his home province.

sentences.zh: 及貴達，不復請歸，至是乃還供養。

translations.literal: After he rose to wealth and eminence he no longer asked to return; only now did he go back to provide for them.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen to wealth and rank he no longer asked to return home; only now did he go back to support them.

sentences.zh: 數年，遭母憂。

translations.literal: Several years later he suffered his mother's bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his mother died.

sentences.zh: 母鉅鹿曹氏，有孝性，夫氏去家，路踰百里，每得魚肉菜果珍美口實者，必令僮僕走奉其母，乃後食焉。

translations.literal: His mother, née Cao of Julu, had filial nature; the husband's household was more than a hundred li from her home. Whenever fish, meat, vegetables, fruit, or delicacies of fine taste arrived, she always made servants run to present them to her mother-in-law, and only afterward ate herself.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, née Cao of Julu, was deeply filial. Her husband's family lived more than a hundred li away; whenever choice fish, meat, vegetables, or fruit arrived, she sent servants running to deliver them to her mother-in-law before she herself would eat.

sentences.zh: 琛母服未闋，復喪父。

translations.literal: Before Chen had completed mourning for his mother, his father also died.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chen had finished mourning his mother, his father died as well.

sentences.zh: 琛於塋兆之內，手種松栢，隆冬之月，負掘水土。

translations.literal: Within the grave mound precinct Chen personally planted pines and cypresses; in the depths of winter he shouldered shovels to dig earth and move soil.
translations.idiomatic: Within the grave precinct Chen planted pines and cypresses with his own hands; in the depths of winter he shouldered shovels to move earth and soil.

sentences.zh: 鄉老哀之，咸助加力。

translations.literal: The village elders pitied him and all helped add their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The village elders took pity on him and all lent their strength.

sentences.zh: 十餘年中，墳成木茂。

translations.literal: Within more than ten years the tomb was complete and the trees flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Within a dozen years the tomb was finished and the trees flourished.

sentences.zh: 與弟僧林誓以同居沒齒。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Senglin he vowed to dwell together to the end of their lives.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Senglin vowed to live together for life.

sentences.zh: 專事產業，躬親農圃，時以鷹犬馳逐自娛。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to managing property, personally tending fields and gardens, and from time to time amused himself hunting with hawk and hound.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to managing the estate, worked the fields himself, and from time to time amused himself hunting with hawk and hound.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大事，猶上表陳情。

translations.literal: When the court had great affairs he still submitted memorials stating his sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: When the court faced major affairs he still submitted memorials stating his views.

sentences.zh: 久之，復除散騎常侍、領給事黃門侍郎、定州大中正。

translations.literal: After a long while he was again appointed Palace Gentleman in Regular Attendance, concurrently Yellow Gate Gentleman Attendant-in-Waiting, and chief rectifier of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again appointed Regular Attendant Gentleman, concurrently Attendant-in-Waiting of the Yellow Gate, and chief rectifier of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 大見親寵，委以門下庶事，出參尚書，入厠帷幄。

translations.literal: He received great favor and trust, was entrusted with the gate-and-chamber subsidiary affairs, went out to participate in the Secretariat, and entered to attend within the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: He won great favor and trust, was entrusted with gate-and-chamber affairs, attended Secretariat sessions abroad, and entered the inner council.

sentences.zh: 琛，高祖時兼主客郎，迎送蕭賾使彭城劉纉，琛欽其器貌，常歎詠之。

translations.literal: Chen, in Emperor Xiaowen's time, had concurrently served as Master of Guests; when receiving and sending Xiao Ze's envoy Liu Zuan of Pengcheng, Chen admired his bearing and appearance and often sighed and recited in praise.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowen's reign Chen had served concurrently as Master of Guests; when escorting Xiao Ze's envoy Liu Zuan of Pengcheng, Chen admired his bearing and often praised him in verse.

sentences.zh: 纉子晣為朐山戍主，晣死，家屬入洛。

translations.literal: Zuan's son Xi was garrison commander at Xiushan; when Xi died, the family members entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's son Xi had been garrison commander at Xiushan; when Xi died, his family came to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 有女年未二十，琛已六十餘矣，乃納晣女為妻。

translations.literal: There was a daughter not yet twenty, while Chen was already past sixty—he then took Xi's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: She was not yet twenty while Chen was past sixty; he took Xi's daughter as his wife.

sentences.zh: 婚日，詔給厨費，琛深所好悅，世宗時調戲之。

translations.literal: On the wedding day an edict granted kitchen expenses; Chen was deeply pleased and fond of this. In Emperor Xuanwu's time he was teased about it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding day the court granted kitchen expenses; Chen was deeply pleased. In Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was teased about the match.

sentences.zh: 盧昶敗於朐山，詔琛馳驛檢按。

translations.literal: When Lu Chang was defeated at Xiushan, an edict ordered Chen to ride post-horses swiftly to inspect and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Chang was defeated at Xiushan, an edict ordered Chen to ride post-horses and conduct an inspection.

sentences.zh: 遷河南尹，加平南將軍，黃門、中正如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Henan, with added rank General Who Pacifies the South; Yellow Gate and Rectifier posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Intendant of Henan and made General Who Pacifies the South; his Yellow Gate and Rectifier posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 琛表曰：「詩稱『京邑翼翼，四方是則』者，京邑是四方之本，安危所在，不可不清。

translations.literal: Chen memorialized, saying: "The Odes say 'The capital teems with splendor—model for the four quarters.' The capital is the root of the four quarters; safety and danger reside there—it cannot fail to be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Chen submitted a memorial: "The Odes say, 'The capital teems with splendor—a model for the four quarters.' The capital is the root of the realm; safety and danger hinge upon it. It cannot fail to be kept in order.

sentences.zh: 是以國家居代，患多盜竊，世祖太武皇帝親自發憤，廣置主司、里宰，皆以下代令長及五等散男有經略者乃得為之。

translations.literal: Therefore when the state was at Dai the affliction was largely banditry and theft; the Shizu, Grand Emperor Taiwu, personally set his mind ablaze, broadly establishing chief offices and ward heads—all had to be district magistrates of the lowering generation and fifth-rank dispersed males with strategic capacity before they could hold these posts.
translations.idiomatic: When the state was at Dai, theft and banditry were rampant. Emperor Taiwu personally took the matter in hand and broadly established chief offices and ward heads, appointing only district magistrates of the lower ranks and fifth-rank dispersed males with proven capacity for strategy.

sentences.zh: 又多置吏士，為其羽翼，崇而重之，始得禁止。

translations.literal: He also placed many clerks and officers as their wings, exalted and weighted them, and only then could he achieve prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He also assigned many clerks and officers as their support, exalted their authority, and only then achieved effective prohibition.

sentences.zh: 今遷都已來，天下轉廣，四遠赴會，事過代都，五方雜沓，難可備簡，寇盜公行，劫害不絕，此由諸坊混雜，釐比不精，主司闇弱，不堪檢察故也。

translations.literal: Now since the move of the capital the realm has grown broader, the four distant quarters hasten to gather, affairs surpass the dynastic capital, the five directions mixed and tangled—hard to prepare and sift; bandits go openly, plunder and harm unceasing—this is because the wards are mixed and confused, apportionment and comparison are not exact, the chief offices are dim and weak and cannot bear inspection and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Since the move of the capital the realm has grown vast, distant regions converge here, and affairs exceed what the old capital knew. The five directions crowd together beyond easy oversight; bandits operate openly and robbery never ceases. This is because wards are jumbled, household registers imprecise, and chief officers too weak to conduct effective inspection.

sentences.zh: 凡使人攻堅木者，必為之擇良器。

translations.literal: Whenever one sends men to attack hard timber, one must for them select fine tools.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever would cut hard timber must first choose the right tools.

sentences.zh: 今河南郡是陛下天山之堅木，盤根錯節，亂植其中。

translations.literal: Now Henan commandery is Your Majesty's hard timber of the Heavenly Mountain—roots interlocked, knots crossed, disorder planted within.
translations.idiomatic: Henan commandery is Your Majesty's hardwood from the Heavenly Mountain—roots tangled, knots crossed, disorder growing within.

sentences.zh: 六部里尉即攻堅之利器，非貞剛精銳，無以治之。

translations.literal: The six-ward district wardens are the sharp tools for attacking hardness; unless upright, firm, keen, and sharp they cannot govern it.
translations.idiomatic: The six-ward district wardens are the sharp tools for such work; unless they are upright, firm, and keen, the capital cannot be governed.

sentences.zh: 今擇尹既非南金，里尉鉛刀而割，欲望清肅都邑，不可得也。

translations.literal: Now the Intendant chosen is not southern gold; the district wardens are lead knives making the cut—desiring to clear and discipline the capital, it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The Intendant now chosen is no southern gold; the district wardens are lead knives attempting the cut. To expect a cleared and disciplined capital is impossible.

sentences.zh: 里正乃流外四品，職輕任碎，多是下才，人懷苟且，不能督察，故使盜得容姦，百賦失理。

translations.literal: The ward chiefs are only fourth rank outside the flow—office light, duty fragmented, mostly low talent; people harbor laxity and cannot supervise and inspect, so bandits gain room for treachery and the hundred levies lose propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Ward chiefs rank only fourth class outside the regular hierarchy; their duties are light and fragmented, and most appointees lack talent. Men grow lax and cannot supervise effectively, so bandits find room for treachery and the hundred levies fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 邊外小縣，所領不過百戶，而令長皆以將軍居之。

translations.literal: In distant border small counties what they administer is no more than a hundred households, yet magistrates and elders all dwell in them with general rank.
translations.idiomatic: In distant border counties the population may not exceed a hundred households, yet magistrates hold general's rank.

sentences.zh: 京邑諸坊，大者或千戶、五百戶，其中皆王公卿尹，貴勢姻戚，豪猾僕隸，蔭養姦徒，高門邃宇，不可干問。

translations.literal: In the capital's wards, the large may have a thousand or five hundred households; within are dukes, princes, ministers, prefects, noble power and affinal kin, fierce and crafty servants and slaves, sheltering and rearing villainous ruffians—high gates, deep courtyards, not to be approached with inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Capital wards may hold five hundred or a thousand households, sheltering dukes, princes, ministers, and prefects, noble kin and affinal connections, fierce servants and slaves who harbor ruffians behind high gates and deep courts beyond ordinary inquiry.

sentences.zh: 又有州郡俠客，蔭結貴遊，附黨連羣，陰為市劫，比之邊縣，難易不同。

translations.literal: There are also provincial and commandery knights-errant who shelter ties with noble wanderers, attach to factions and link in groups, secretly conducting marketplace robbery—compared with border counties, the difficulty and ease differ.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery knights-errant also shelter ties with noble wanderers, form factions, and conduct secret marketplace robbery. Compared with border counties, the difficulty is altogether different.

sentences.zh: 今難彼易此，實為未愜。

translations.literal: Now making hard there and easy here—truly not satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: To make the hard post easy and the easy post hard is plainly unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 王者立法，隨時從宜，改弦易調，明主所急。

translations.literal: Kings who establish law follow the times and accord with suitability; changing the strings and altering the tuning—the enlightened ruler's urgent matter.
translations.idiomatic: Kings who make law adapt it to the times; retuning the strings is what an enlightened ruler urgently requires.

sentences.zh: 先朝立品，不必即定，施而觀之，不便則改。

translations.literal: The former court established grades—not necessarily fixed at once; implement and observe them; if inconvenient then change.
translations.idiomatic: The former court established grades without fixing them forever: implement, observe, and change what proves inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 今閑官靜任，猶聽長兼，況煩劇要務，不得簡能下領？

translations.literal: Now idle offices and quiet commissions still permit concurrent long tenure—how much more urgent, vexing key duties that cannot delegate simplified talent for lower leadership?
translations.idiomatic: Even idle offices still permit long concurrent tenure—how much less may urgent and taxing duties be left to unqualified subordinates?

sentences.zh: 請取武官中八品將軍已下幹用貞濟者，以本官俸恤，領里尉之任，各食其祿，高者領六部尉，中者領經途尉，下者領里正。

translations.literal: Request to take from military officers of eighth rank and below, down to general, those of capable loyalty and purity, pay them with their original office salary and allowance, and let them hold district warden duties; each eating his stipend—higher leading six-ward wardens, middle leading main-road wardens, lower leading ward chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that capable and upright military officers of eighth rank and below, down to general, be paid from their original salaries and assigned as district wardens at their respective stipends: the higher to lead six-ward wardens, the middle main-road wardens, the lower ward chiefs.

sentences.zh: 不爾，請少高里尉之品，選下品中應遷之者，進而為之。

translations.literal: If not so, request slightly raising ward warden grades, selecting from lower grades those who should be transferred, advancing them to the posts.
translations.idiomatic: If not, raise the ward warden grades slightly and promote from lower ranks those due for advancement.

sentences.zh: 則督責有所，輦轂可清。

translations.literal: Then supervision and responsibility would have a place; the imperial carriage district could be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Then supervision would have force and the imperial capital could be cleared.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「里正可進至勳品，經途從九品，六部尉正九品諸職中簡取，何必須武人也？

translations.literal: " An edict stated: "Ward chiefs may advance to merit grades; main-road from ninth grade; six-ward wardens selected from regular ninth-grade offices among the ranks—why must they be military men?
translations.idiomatic: " An edict replied: "Ward chiefs may advance to merit grades; main-road wardens from ninth grade; six-ward wardens chosen from ninth-grade offices in the regular hierarchy—why must they be military men?

sentences.zh: 」琛又奏以羽林為遊軍，於諸坊巷司察盜賊。

translations.literal: " Chen further memorialized using the Feathered Forest as roaming troops to inspect and watch for bandits in all wards and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen further memorialized to use the Feathered Forest as roaming patrols to watch for bandits in all wards and lanes.

sentences.zh: 於是京邑清靜，至今踵焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the capital was cleared and tranquil—to this day they follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the capital grew calm and orderly, and the practice endures to this day.

sentences.zh: 轉太子少保，黃門如故。

translations.literal: Transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Yellow Gate as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent while retaining his Yellow Gate post.

sentences.zh: 大將軍高肇伐蜀，以琛為使持節、假撫軍將軍，領步騎四萬為前驅都督。

translations.literal: When Grand General Gao Zhao campaigned against Shu, Chen was made bearer of the staff of authority with acting rank General Who Pacifies the Army, leading forty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Gao Zhao campaigned against Shu, Chen was made bearer of the staff of authority and acting General Who Pacifies the Army, commanding forty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 琛次梁州獠亭，會世宗崩，班師。

translations.literal: Chen halted at Liang province, Liaoting; he encountered Emperor Xuanwu's death and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen halted at Liaoting in Liang province; when Emperor Xuanwu died, the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高肇既死，以琛，肇之黨也，不宜復參朝政，出為營州刺史，加安北將軍。

translations.literal: After Gao Zhao died, because Chen was Zhao's faction-mate he should not again participate in court governance; he was sent out as Inspector of Ying province, with added rank General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Zhao's death, because Chen had been his faction-mate he was deemed unfit to resume court politics and was sent out as Inspector of Ying province with the added rank General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以光祿大夫李思穆代之，時年六十五矣，遂停中山，久之乃赴洛。

translations.literal: After more than a year Li Simu, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, replaced him; he was then sixty-five, stopped at Zhongshan, and only after a long while went to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year Li Simu, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, replaced him. Chen was then sixty-five; he lingered at Zhongshan and only after a long while went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 除鎮西將軍、涼州刺史，猶以琛高氏之昵也，不欲處之於內。

translations.literal: Appointed General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Liang province—still because Chen was intimate with the Gao clan, they did not wish to place him within the interior.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Liang province; because Chen remained intimate with the Gao clan, the court still did not wish to keep him within the interior.

sentences.zh: 尋徵拜太常卿，仍以本將軍出為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonials, still with his original general's rank sent out as Inspector of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonials, then sent out as Inspector of Xu province with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 及入辭肅宗，琛辭以老，詔除吏部尚書，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When he entered to take leave of Emperor Xiaoming, Chen declined on grounds of age; an edict appointed him Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave of Emperor Xiaoming, Chen pleaded old age; an edict appointed him Minister of the Ministry of Personnel while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除征北將軍、定州刺史，衣錦晝遊，大為稱滿。

translations.literal: Before long appointed General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Ding province—embroidered robes by day, roaming homeward, greatly admired and satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Ding province, returning home in embroidered robes by day to universal admiration and satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 治體嚴細，甚無聲譽。

translations.literal: His governance was stern and minute; he had very little reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was stern and meticulous, but he won little reputation.

sentences.zh: 崔光辭司徒之授也，琛與光書，外相抑揚，內實附會也。

translations.literal: When Cui Guang declined acceptance of the Minister of the Masses, Chen exchanged letters with Guang—outwardly mutually restraining and elevating, inwardly truly joining in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Guang declined appointment as Minister of the Masses, Chen exchanged letters with him—outwardly modest praise and restraint, inwardly true collusion.

sentences.zh: 光亦揣其意，復書褒美以悅之。

translations.literal: Guang also inferred his intent and wrote back with praise and beauty to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also divined his intent and wrote back with flattering praise to please him.

sentences.zh: 徵為車騎將軍、特進，又拜侍中。

translations.literal: Summoned as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Special Grand Master; again appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Special Grand Master, and again appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以其衰老，詔賜御府杖，朝直杖以出入。

translations.literal: Because of his aging decline, an edict bestowed the imperial storehouse staff; for morning attendance he used the staff to enter and exit.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his advanced age, an edict granted him an imperial staff, which he used when attending court.

sentences.zh: 正光五年冬卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Zhenguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year of Zhenguang he died.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢十萬、物七百段、蠟三百斤。

translations.literal: An edict granted eastern garden secret vessels, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, one hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of goods, three hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted eastern-garden funeral vessels, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, one hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of goods, and three hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒公、尚書左僕射，加後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Duke of the Masses, Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, with added rear guard musical accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the Masses and Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, with rear-guard musical accompaniment added.

sentences.zh: 太常議諡「文穆」。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Ceremonials deliberated posthumous title "Wenmu" (Cultivated and Solemn).
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Ceremonials proposed the posthumous title Wenmu (Cultivated and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 吏部郎袁翻奏曰：「案禮：諡者，行之迹也；

translations.literal: Yuan Fan of the Ministry of Personnel memorialized, saying: "According to the Rites: a posthumous name is the trace of conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fan of the Ministry of Personnel memorialized: "According to the Rites, a posthumous name is the trace of conduct;

sentences.zh: 號者，功之表也；

translations.literal: a title is the manifestation of achievement;
translations.idiomatic: a title is the manifestation of achievement;

sentences.zh: 車服者，位之章也。

translations.literal: chariots and robes are the insignia of rank.
translations.idiomatic: chariots and robes are the insignia of rank.

sentences.zh: 是以大行受大名，細行受細名。

translations.literal: Therefore the great conduct receives a great name, the small conduct a small name.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore great conduct receives a great name and small conduct a small name.

sentences.zh: 行生於己，名生於人，故闔棺然後定諡。

translations.literal: Conduct arises in oneself; the name arises in others; therefore only when the coffin is closed is the posthumous name fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct arises in oneself, but the name arises in others; therefore the posthumous name is fixed only when the coffin is closed.

sentences.zh: 皆累其生時美惡，所以為將來勸戒，身雖死，使名常存也。

translations.literal: All accumulate the beauty and ugliness of his living time, thereby for the future to admonish and warn—though the body dies, yet the name is always kept.
translations.idiomatic: All accumulate the good and ill of his lifetime to admonish posterity; though the body dies, the name endures.

sentences.zh: 凡薨亡者，屬所即言大鴻臚，移本郡大中正，條其行迹功過，承中正移言公府，下太常部博士評議，為諡列上。

translations.literal: For all who die of illness, the subordinate office immediately informs the Grand Herald; it is transmitted to the home commandery's chief rectifier to itemize conduct, achievement, and fault; the rectifier transmits to the public offices; down to the Ministry of Ceremonials' departmental erudites to debate and establish the posthumous name listed upward.
translations.idiomatic: For all who die, the subordinate office reports to the Grand Herald, who transmits the case to the home commandery's chief rectifier to itemize conduct, achievements, and faults; the rectifier forwards this to the public offices, and the Ministry of Ceremonials' erudites debate and propose the posthumous name for submission.

sentences.zh: 諡不應法者，博士坐如選舉不以實論。

translations.literal: When the posthumous name does not accord with law, the erudite is punished like recommendation in selection without truth.
translations.idiomatic: When a posthumous name fails to accord with law, the erudite is punished as for a false recommendation in selection.

sentences.zh: 若行狀失實，中正坐如博士。

translations.literal: If the conduct record is not factual, the rectifier is punished like the erudite.
translations.idiomatic: If the conduct record is false, the rectifier is punished like the erudite.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王莫不殷勤重慎，以為褒貶之實也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity emperors and kings have all been earnest and heavily cautious, taking this as the substance of praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity emperors and kings have all been earnest and cautious, treating this as the substance of praise and blame.

sentences.zh: 今之行狀，皆出自其家，任其臣子自言君父之行，無復相是非之事。

translations.literal: Today's conduct records all come from their own families, allowing their ministers and sons freely to speak the ruler-father's conduct—no more mutual right-and-wrong matters.
translations.idiomatic: Today's conduct records all come from the deceased's own family, allowing sons and ministers to describe the father's conduct at will, with no further scrutiny of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 臣子之欲光揚君父，但苦迹之不高，行之不美，是以極辭肆意，無復限量。

translations.literal: Ministers and sons wishing to glorify the ruler-father only suffer that the traces are not lofty and conduct not beautiful; therefore they use extreme rhetoric at will without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and ministers wishing to glorify their father lament only that his deeds were not lofty and his conduct not beautiful; therefore they use extravagant rhetoric without limit.

sentences.zh: 觀其狀也，則周孔聯鑣，伊顏接袵；

translations.literal: Viewing their records, then Zhou and Kong yoke their chariots together, Yi and Yan join their robes;
translations.idiomatic: Read their records and Zhou and Confucius seem to yoke chariots together, Yi Yin and Yan Hui to share one robe;

sentences.zh: 論其諡也，雖窮文盡武，罔或加焉。

translations.literal: discussing their posthumous names, even exhausting wen and wu in text, none could be added.
translations.idiomatic: yet for their posthumous names, even the fullest wen and wu epithets could add nothing more.

sentences.zh: 然今之博士與古不同，唯知依其行狀，又先問其家人之意，臣子所求，便為議上，都不復斟酌與奪，商量是非。

translations.literal: Yet today's erudites differ from antiquity—they only know to follow the conduct record, and again first ask the family's intent; whatever ministers and sons request they then debate upward, none again weighing grant and denial or negotiating right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today's erudites differ from antiquity: they merely follow the conduct record, first ask the family's wishes, and submit whatever sons and ministers request, no longer weighing grant or denial or debating right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 致號諡之加，與汎階莫異，專以極美為稱，無復貶降之名，禮官之失，一至於此！

translations.literal: Causing posthumous titles to be added no different from general ranks, exclusively using utmost beauty as title without names of demotion and lowering—the rites officers' failure reached this point!
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous titles have become no different from general promotions, using only the most flattering names with none of demotion or lowering. The failure of the rites officers has reached this point!

sentences.zh: 案甄司徒行狀，至德與聖人齊蹤，鴻名共大賢比跡，『文穆』之諡，何足加焉。

translations.literal: Investigating Minister Zhen's conduct record—supreme virtue treads equal with sages, great fame shares traces with great worthies—how is the posthumous name "Wenmu" adequate to be added?
translations.idiomatic: Review Minister Zhen's conduct record: supreme virtue walks equal with sages, great fame shares traces with great worthies—how can the posthumous name Wenmu even be adequate, let alone added to?

sentences.zh: 但比來贈諡，於例普重，如甄琛之流，無不複諡。

translations.literal: But recently posthumous gifts have universally been heavy in precedent; men like Zhen Chen without exception received posthumous names again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently posthumous enfeoffments have been universally lavish; men like Zhen Chen without exception receive posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 謂宜依諡法『慈惠愛民曰孝』，宜諡曰孝穆公。

translations.literal: I deem it fitting according to posthumous law "kind and gracious, loving the people is called Xiao"—the posthumous name should be Duke Xiao-Mu.
translations.idiomatic: I deem it fitting, according to posthumous law, that 'kind and gracious, loving the people is called Xiao,' to posthumously name him Duke Xiao-Mu.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，明勒太常、司徒有行狀如此，言辭流宕，無復節限者，悉請裁量，不聽為受。

translations.literal: From now afterward, clearly charge the Ministry of Ceremonials and Minister of the Masses that when conduct records are like this, language floating and unbounded without limits—all request judgment and measurement, not permitted to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, clearly charge the Ministry of Ceremonials and the Minister of the Masses that when conduct records are like this, language unbounded and without limit, all such cases are to be judged and not accepted.

sentences.zh: 必準人立諡，不得甚加優越。

translations.literal: Must standardize on the man in establishing posthumous names; cannot greatly add superiority.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous names must be fitted to the man; they must not be greatly inflated.

sentences.zh: 復仍踵前來之失者，付法司科罪。

translations.literal: Those who again follow the former errors—hand over to the law offices for punishment by statute.
translations.idiomatic: Those who again repeat these former errors are to be handed to the law offices for punishment.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 琛祖載，肅宗親送，降車就輿，弔服哭之，遣舍人慰其諸子。

translations.literal: When Chen's coffin was borne, Emperor Xiaoming personally escorted, descended from the carriage to approach the bier, wore mourning and wept for him, and dispatched a chamberlain to console his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen's coffin was borne, Emperor Xiaoming personally escorted it, descended from his carriage to approach the bier, wore mourning and wept, and sent a chamberlain to console his sons.

sentences.zh: 琛性輕簡，好嘲謔，故少風望。

translations.literal: Chen's nature was light and easy; he loved banter and mockery, therefore he had little esteem and prospect.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was light and easy by nature and loved banter and mockery, and therefore won little public esteem.

sentences.zh: 然明解有幹具，在官清白。

translations.literal: Yet he was clear in understanding and had executive capacity; in office he was pure and white.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was clear-minded and capable, and in office remained scrupulously clean.

sentences.zh: 自高祖、世宗咸相知待，肅宗以師傅之義而加禮焉。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xuanwu he was all known and treated well; Emperor Xiaoming because of the mentor's bond added ritual toward him.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xuanwu he was known and favored; Emperor Xiaoming, because of their bond as teacher and pupil, showed him added courtesy.

sentences.zh: 所著文章，鄙碎無大體，時有理詣，磔四聲、姓族廢興、會通緇素三論，及家誨二十篇，篤學文一卷，頗行於世。

translations.literal: His written works were coarse and fragmentary without great structure; occasionally there was rational penetration—"Dissecting the Four Tones," "Rise and Fall of Clans and Surnames," "Meeting and Communicating Black and White" three treatises, and twenty chapters of family admonitions, one roll of "Sincere Learning Literature," all rather circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were coarse and fragmentary, without great structure, though occasionally penetrating: three treatises titled Dissecting the Four Tones, Rise and Fall of Clans and Surnames, and Meeting and Communicating Black and White; twenty chapters of family admonitions; and one roll of Sincere Learning Literature—all circulated rather widely.

sentences.zh: 琛長子侃，字道正。

translations.literal: Chen's eldest son Kan, style name Daozheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's eldest son was Kan, courtesy name Daozheng.

sentences.zh: 郡功曹，釋褐祕書郎。

translations.literal: Commandery Merit Officer; on leaving the sack-cloth he was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commandery Merit Officer and, upon first entering office, was made Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 性險薄，多與盜劫交通。

translations.literal: His nature was treacherous and shallow; he often associated with bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: By nature treacherous and shallow, he consorted freely with bandits and robbers.

sentences.zh: 隨琛在京，以酒色夜宿洛水亭舍，毆擊主人，為司州所劾，淹在州獄，琛大以慚慨。

translations.literal: Following Chen in the capital, because of wine and women he lodged overnight at a Luoshui pavilion inn, beat the proprietor, was impeached by the metropolitan office, lingered long in the provincial prison—Chen was deeply ashamed and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying Chen in the capital, he spent a night carousing at a Lu River pavilion lodge, beat the innkeeper, and was impeached by the metropolitan office. He lingered in provincial prison, to Chen's deep shame and distress.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷為牧，與琛先不協，欲具案窮推。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Guangping was regional governor; he had long been at odds with Chen and wished to prosecute the case fully and press the investigation to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Guangping was regional governor; already at odds with Chen, he wished to pursue the case to its fullest extent.

sentences.zh: 琛託左右以聞，世宗遣白衣吳仲安敕懷寬放，懷固執治之。

translations.literal: Chen entrusted his intimates to report it; Emperor Xuanwu dispatched unranked messenger Wu Zhong'an to charge Huai to release him leniently, but Huai obstinately prosecuted the case.
translations.idiomatic: Chen used his intimates to report the matter; Emperor Xuanwu sent unranked messenger Wu Zhong'an to order Huai to release him, but Huai insisted on prosecuting the case.

sentences.zh: 久乃特旨出之。

translations.literal: Only after a long while was he released by special edict.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he freed by special imperial order.

sentences.zh: 侃自此沉廢，卒於家。

translations.literal: Kan from this sank into obsolescence and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Kan sank into obscurity thereafter and died at home.

sentences.zh: 侃弟楷，字德方。

translations.literal: Kan's younger brother Kai, style name Defang.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's younger brother was Kai, courtesy name Defang.

sentences.zh: 粗有文學，頗習吏事。

translations.literal: He had rough literary learning and was fairly practiced in clerkly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had some literary learning and was fairly adept at official business.

sentences.zh: 太平中，[2]上高祖頌十二篇，文多不載，優詔報之。

translations.literal: In the Taiping era he presented twelve odes to Emperor Xiaowen; most of the texts were not recorded, and a favorable edict responded.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiping era he presented twelve odes to Emperor Xiaowen; most of the texts were not preserved in the record, but the court replied with a favorable edict.

sentences.zh: 琛啟除祕書郎。

translations.literal: Chen memorialized to remove him from the post of Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Chen memorialized to have him dismissed as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩未葬，楷與河南尹丞張普惠等飲戲，免官。

translations.literal: Before Emperor Xuanwu was buried, Kai drank and played games with Zhang Puhui, deputy of the Intendant of Henan, and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor Xuanwu was buried, Kai caroused and played drinking games with Zhang Puhui, deputy of the Intendant of Henan, and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄為司徒，引為公曹參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng became Minister of the Masses and recruited him as Bureau Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Cheng of Rencheng became Minister of the Masses, he recruited Kai as Bureau Aide.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書儀曹郎，有當官之稱。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bureau and had a reputation for fitness in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bureau and won a reputation for competence in office.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，定州刺史、廣陽王淵被徵還朝，時楷丁憂在鄉，淵臨發，召楷兼長史，[3]委以州任。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Yuan Yuan, Prince of Guangyang and Inspector of Ding province, was summoned back to court. Kai was then in mourning in the countryside; on the eve of Yuan's departure he summoned Kai as acting Chief Administrator and entrusted him with the province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Yuan Yuan, Prince of Guangyang and Inspector of Ding province, was summoned back to court. Kai was then in mourning in the countryside; on the eve of Yuan's departure he summoned Kai as acting Chief Administrator and entrusted him with the province.

sentences.zh: 尋值鮮于脩禮、毛普賢等率北鎮流民反於州西北之左人城，屠村掠野，引向州城。

translations.literal: Soon Xianyu Xiuli, Mao Puxian, and others led displaced northerners from the northern garrisons to rebel at Zuoren Fort northwest of the province, slaughtering villages and pillaging the countryside as they advanced on the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianyu Xiuli, Mao Puxian, and others led displaced northerners from the northern garrisons to rebel at Zuoren Fort northwest of the province, slaughtering villages and pillaging the countryside as they advanced on the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 州城之內，先有燕恒雲三州避難之戶，皆依傍市鄽，草廬攅住。

translations.literal: Within the city were earlier refugee households from Yan, Heng, and Yun provinces, all clustered in thatched huts along the market lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city were earlier refugees from Yan, Heng, and Yun provinces, all clustered in shanties along the market lanes.

sentences.zh: 脩禮等聲云欲收此輩，共為舉動。

translations.literal: Xiuli and the others proclaimed that they meant to gather these people into a joint uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuli and the others proclaimed that they meant to rally these people into a joint uprising.

sentences.zh: 既外寇將逼，恐有內應，楷見人情不安，慮有變起，乃收州人中粗豪者皆殺之，以威外賊，固城民之心。

translations.literal: With outer enemies closing in and fear of inner collusion, Kai, seeing popular unrest and fearing sudden revolt, seized and killed all the rough and powerful men in the province to awe the outer bandits and steady the hearts of the city's people.
translations.idiomatic: With outer enemies closing in and fear of inner collusion, Kai saw the populace unsettled and feared sudden revolt. He seized and killed all the rough and powerful men in the province to awe the outer bandits and steady the hearts of the city's people.

sentences.zh: 及刺史元固、[4]大都督楊津等至，楷乃還家。

translations.literal: When Inspector Yuan Gu and Grand Commander Yang Jin arrived, Kai then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Yuan Gu and Grand Commander Yang Jin arrived, Kai returned home.

sentences.zh: 後脩禮等忿楷屠害北人，遂掘其父墓，載棺巡城，示相報復。

translations.literal: Later Xiuli and the others, enraged at Kai's slaughter of northerners, dug up his father's tomb, paraded the coffin around the walls, and displayed revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiuli and the others, enraged at Kai's slaughter of northerners, dug up his father's tomb, paraded the coffin around the city walls, and displayed their intent to repay him in kind.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，徵為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he was summoned as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死，帝以其堪率鄉義，除試守常山太守，賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: On Erzhu Rong's death the emperor deemed him fit to rally village loyalty and appointed him acting Administrator of Changshan, granting two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On Erzhu Rong's death the emperor deemed him fit to rally local loyalty and appointed him acting Administrator of Changshan, granting two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，除征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，遷衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Chu's reign he was appointed General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal, then transferred to General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Chu's reign he was made General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal, then transferred to General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王取為儀同府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang of Qi took him as Advisory Aide of the Equipage Office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi took him on as Advisory Aide of the Equipage Office.

sentences.zh: 天平四年卒，年四十六。
