translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Tianping, age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianping, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎將軍、祕書監、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed General of Fast Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, and Inspector of Cang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General of Fast Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, and Inspector of Cang province.

sentences.zh: 楷弟寬，字仁規。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Kuan, style name Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's younger brother was Kuan, courtesy name Rengui.

sentences.zh: 自員外散騎侍郎、本州別駕，稍遷太尉從事中郎、治書侍御史。

translations.literal: From Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and Vice-Prefect of his home province he was gradually promoted to Aide of the Grand Master of War and Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and Vice-Prefect of his home province, he was gradually promoted to Aide of the Grand Master of War and Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 武定初，謝病還鄉，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the start of Wuding he pleaded illness and returned home, dying there.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wuding he pleaded illness and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 僧林，終於鄉里。

translations.literal: Senglin ended his days in his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Senglin ended his days in his home village.

sentences.zh: 琛從父弟密，字叔雍。

translations.literal: Chen's paternal cousin Mi, style name Shuyong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's paternal cousin was Mi, courtesy name Shuyong.

sentences.zh: 清謹少嗜欲，頗涉書史。

translations.literal: Clear and careful, with few cravings; he had dipped into classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-minded and careful, with few cravings, he had dipped into the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太和中，奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was made Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was made Court Attendant.

sentences.zh: 密疾世俗貪競，乾沒榮寵，曾作風賦以見意。

translations.literal: Mi detested worldly greed and competition, seizing glory and favor; he once wrote a Rhapsody on Wind to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Mi detested worldly greed and the scramble for glory and favor; he once wrote a Rhapsody on Wind to express his views.

sentences.zh: 後參中山王英軍事，英鍾離敗退，鄉人蘇良沒於賊手，密盡私財以贖之。

translations.literal: Later he joined Prince Ying of Zhongshan's staff; when Ying was defeated and withdrew from Zhongli, his townsman Su Liang fell into bandit hands and Mi spent all his private wealth to ransom him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined the staff of Prince Ying of Zhongshan; when Ying was defeated and withdrew from Zhongli, his townsman Su Liang fell into bandit hands, and Mi spent all his private wealth to ransom him.

sentences.zh: 良既歸，傾資報密，密一皆不受，謂良曰：「濟君之日，本不求貨，豈相贖之意也？」

translations.literal: When Liang returned he poured out his wealth to repay Mi; Mi refused every item, saying to Liang: "The day I aided you, I sought no goods—how could this be the meaning of ransom?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liang returned he poured out his wealth to repay Mi; Mi refused every item, saying to Liang, "The day I aided you I sought no reward—how could this be the meaning of ransom?"

sentences.zh: 歷太尉鎧曹，遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He served in the Grand Commander's armory bureau and was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Grand Commander's armory bureau and was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，通直散騎常侍、冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was Regular Attendant of the Secretariat in Direct Communication and General Who Champions.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was Regular Attendant of the Secretariat in Direct Communication and General Who Champions.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥葛榮侵擾河北，裴衍、源子邕敗沒，人情不安，詔密為相州行臺，援守鄴城。

translations.literal: When bandit chief Ge Rong harried Hebei and Pei Yan and Yuan Ziyin were defeated and lost, popular morale was unsettled; an edict made Mi mobile prefect of Xiang province to aid in defending Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit chief Ge Rong harried Hebei and Pei Yan and Yuan Ziyin were defeated and lost, morale was unsettled; an edict appointed Mi mobile prefect of Xiang province to aid in defending Ye.

sentences.zh: 莊帝以密全鄴之勳，賞安市縣開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang, for Mi's merit in holding Ye, granted him Marquis of a county at Anshi with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang, for Mi's merit in holding Ye, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anshi county with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷平東將軍、光祿大夫，領廷尉少卿，尋轉征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, heading Vice Minister of Justice; soon transferred to General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, heading Vice Minister of Justice; soon he was transferred to General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，車騎將軍、廷尉卿，在官有平直之譽。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Justice, with a reputation for uprightness in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Justice, with a reputation for uprightness in office.

sentences.zh: 出為北徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of North Xu, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of North Xu, his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 興和四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎將軍、儀同三司、瀛州刺史，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed General of Fast Cavalry, equal to the Three Departments, Inspector of Ying province, posthumous title Jing (Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General of Fast Cavalry, equal to the Three Departments, and Inspector of Ying province, with the posthumous title Jing (Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 長子儉，字元恭。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jian, style name Yuangong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Jian, courtesy name Yuangong.

sentences.zh: 官至前將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: His offices reached Front General and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Front General and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 儉弟賾，有才學，亦早卒。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Ze had literary talent and also died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Ze had literary talent and also died young.

sentences.zh: 纂頗涉經史，雅有氣尚，交結勝流。

translations.literal: Zuan had dipped into classics and histories, had refined spirit and bearing, and associated with eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had dipped into the classics and histories, possessed refined spirit and bearing, and associated with eminent men.

sentences.zh: 太和中，釋褐奉朝請，稍遷伏波將軍、任城王澄鎮北府騎兵參軍，帶魏昌縣令，吏民安之。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, on first entering office he was made Court Attendant; he was gradually promoted to General Who Quells Waves and Cavalry Aide in Prince Cheng of Rencheng's northern commandery staff, concurrently Magistrate of Wei County, and officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era, upon first entering office he was made Court Attendant; he was gradually promoted to General Who Quells Waves and Cavalry Aide on Prince Cheng of Rencheng's northern staff, concurrently Magistrate of Wei County, where officials and people lived at peace under him.

sentences.zh: 後為北中府司馬，久之，除樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Marshal of the North Central Headquarters; after a long while he was appointed Prefect of Yueling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Marshal of the North Central Headquarters; after a long interval he was appointed Prefect of Yueling.

sentences.zh: 在郡多所受納，聞御史至，棄郡逃走，於是除名，乃卒。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he took many bribes; hearing the censor had arrived, he abandoned the prefecture and fled, was struck from the rolls, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture he took many bribes; when he heard the censor had arrived, he abandoned his post and fled, was struck from the rolls, and then died.

sentences.zh: 天平初，贈使持節、都督冀定二州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Tianping he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Ji and Ding provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, and Inspector of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianping he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Ji and Ding provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, and Inspector of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 纂叔感，字崇仁。

translations.literal: Zuan's uncle Gan, style name Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's uncle was Gan, courtesy name Chongren.

sentences.zh: 有器業，不應州郡之命。

translations.literal: He had capacity and achievement and did not respond to summons from provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He had capacity and achievement and did not respond to summons from provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 子宣軌，少孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: The man Xuangui, orphaned young, served his mother with famed filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangui, orphaned young, served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 歷郡功曹、州主簿。

translations.literal: He served as commandery Merit Officer and provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commandery Merit Officer and provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，釋褐奉朝請、冀州征東府長流參軍，轉相州中軍府錄事參軍，定州別駕。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era, on first entering office he was Court Attendant and long-flow aide in Ji's eastern campaign headquarters; he transferred to recorder in Xiang province's central army headquarters and became Vice-Prefect of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanchang era, upon first entering office he was made Court Attendant and long-flow aide in Ji's eastern campaign headquarters; he transferred to recorder in Xiang province's central army headquarters and became Vice-Prefect of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮遠將軍、員外散騎常侍，出為相州撫軍府司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Guards the Far and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and was sent out as Marshal of Xiang province's Pacification Army Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Guards the Far and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and was sent out as Marshal of Xiang province's Pacification Army Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 宣軌性通率，輕財好施。

translations.literal: Xuangui's nature was frank and open; he was light with wealth and loved giving.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangui was frank and open by nature, light with wealth, and generous in giving.

sentences.zh: 屬葛榮圍城，與刺史李神有固守之効。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong besieged the city, together with Inspector Li Shen he had merit in steadfast defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong besieged the city, he and Inspector Li Shen won merit for steadfast defense.

sentences.zh: 永安中，以功賜爵中山公。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era, for merit he was granted the noble rank Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongan era, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 中興初，坐事，死於鄴。

translations.literal: Early in Zhongxing he was punished for an offense and died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhongxing he was punished for an offense and died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 子子瑜。

translations.literal: His son Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 纂從弟元賓，太和十六年，出身奉朝請，遷員外郎、給事中。

translations.literal: Zuan's cousin Yuanbin, in the sixteenth year of Taihe on first entering office was made Court Attendant, then promoted to Supernumerary Gentleman and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's cousin Yuanbin, in the sixteenth year of Taihe upon first entering office was made Court Attendant, then promoted to Supernumerary Gentleman and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 正光中，除中堅將軍、射聲校尉。

translations.literal: In Zhenguang he was appointed General Firm Center and Colonel of the Shooting-Sound Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguang he was appointed General Firm Center and Colonel of the Shooting-Sound Corps.

sentences.zh: 永安三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Yongan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Yongan.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，外生高敖曹貴達，啟贈持節、撫軍將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yongxi his maternal nephew Gao Aocao rose high and memorialized posthumous grant of bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi his maternal nephew Gao Aocao rose to power and memorialized a posthumous grant of bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 子辨，天平中，司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Bian, in the Tianping era, was Runner Aide to the Minister of the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bian, in the Tianping era, was Runner Aide to the Minister of the Masses.

sentences.zh: 高聰，字僧智，本勃海蓨人。

translations.literal: Gao Cong, style name Sengzhi, was originally a man of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cong, courtesy name Sengzhi, was originally from Tiao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖軌，隨慕容德徙青州，因居北海之劇縣。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gui followed Murong De to Qingzhou and thus dwelt in Juxian of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gui followed Murong De to Qingzhou and thus settled in Juxian of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 父法昂，劉駿車騎將軍王玄謨甥也。

translations.literal: His father Fa'ang was nephew by marriage to Liu Jun's General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Xuomo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fa'ang was nephew by marriage to Liu Jun's General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Xuomo.

sentences.zh: 少隨玄謨征伐，以軍功至員外郎。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Xuomo on campaigns and by military merit reached Supernumerary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he followed Xuomo on campaigns and by military merit rose to Supernumerary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 聰生而喪母，祖母王撫育之。

translations.literal: Cong was born having lost his mother; his grandmother Wang raised him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong lost his mother at birth; his grandmother Wang raised him.

sentences.zh: 大軍攻克東陽，聰徙入平城，與蔣少遊為雲中兵戶，窘困無所不至。

translations.literal: When the grand army took Dongyang, Cong was moved into Pingcheng; with Jiang Shaoyou he became a Yunzhong military household and knew privation in every form.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand army took Dongyang, Cong was moved to Pingcheng; with Jiang Shaoyou he was registered as a Yunzhong military household and suffered every kind of privation.

sentences.zh: 族祖允視之若孫，大加賙給。

translations.literal: His clan elder Yun treated him as a grandson and greatly bestowed relief upon him.
translations.idiomatic: His clan elder Yun treated him as a grandson and gave him generous relief.

sentences.zh: 聰涉獵經史，頗有文才，允嘉之，數稱其美，言之朝廷，云：「青州蔣少遊與從孫僧智，雖為孤弱，然皆有文情。

translations.literal: Cong ranged through classics and histories and had considerable literary talent; Yun rejoiced in him, often praised his gifts, and spoke to the court, saying: "Jiang Shaoyou of Qingzhou and my nephew Sengzhi, though orphaned and weak, yet all have literary sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Cong ranged through the classics and histories and had considerable literary talent; Yun rejoiced in him, often praised his gifts, and spoke to the court, saying, "Jiang Shaoyou of Qingzhou and my nephew Sengzhi, though orphaned and weak, yet both possess literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 」由是與少遊同拜中書博士。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he and Shaoyou were together appointed Erudites of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he and Shaoyou were together appointed Erudites of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 積十年，轉侍郎，以本官為高陽王雍友，稍為高祖知賞。

translations.literal: After ten years he was transferred to Gentleman; with his original rank he became Friend to Prince Yong of Gaoyang and was gradually known and favored by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years he was transferred to Gentleman; retaining his rank he became Friend to Prince Yong of Gaoyang and was gradually noticed and favored by Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，兼員外散騎常侍，使於蕭昭業。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he was concurrently Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and envoy to Xiao Zhaoye.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he served concurrently as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and envoy to Xiao Zhaoye.

sentences.zh: 高祖定都洛陽，追詔聰等曰：「比於河陽敕卿，仍屆瀍洛，周視舊業，依然有懷，固欲先之營之，後乃薄伐。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowen fixed the capital at Luoyang, he followed up with an edict to Cong and the others, saying: "Recently at Heyang I charged you, yet you have now arrived at the Chan and Luo rivers, surveying our former domain—I still feel the pull. I had firmly intended to establish it first and only then undertake a limited campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowen fixed the capital at Luoyang, he sent a follow-up edict to Cong and the others, saying, "Recently at Heyang I charged you, yet you have now arrived at the Chan and Luo rivers and surveyed our former domain—I still feel the pull. I had intended to establish the capital first and only then undertake a limited campaign.

sentences.zh: 且以賾喪甫爾，使通在昔，乘危幸凶，君子弗取。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Xiao Ze's mourning has only just begun and our envoys are still bound by former protocols, to seize upon crisis for advantage is what a gentleman will not take.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Xiao Ze's mourning has only just begun and our envoys are still bound by former protocols, to seize upon crisis for advantage is what a gentleman will not do.

sentences.zh: 是用輟茲前圖，遠期來會，爰息六師，三川是宅，將底居成周，永恢皇宇。

translations.literal: Therefore I set aside this former design, deferring our meeting to a later day; I now rest the six armies and make the Three Rivers our home, intending to settle at Chengzhou and forever restore the imperial realm.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I set aside this former design and defer our meeting to a later day; I now rest the six armies and make the Three Rivers our home, intending to settle at Chengzhou and forever restore the imperial realm.

sentences.zh: 今更造璽書，以代往詔，比所敕授，隨宜變之，善勗皇華，無替指意。

translations.literal: I now compose a fresh imperial letter to replace the former edict; change what I previously conveyed as circumstances require. Fulfill your role as envoys splendidly, and do not betray my intent.
translations.idiomatic: I now compose a fresh imperial letter to replace the former edict; adapt what I previously conveyed as circumstances require. Fulfill your role as envoys splendidly, and do not betray my intent.

sentences.zh: 」使還，遷通直散騎常侍、兼太府少卿，轉兼太子左率。

translations.literal: " On his return from the mission he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Secretariat in Direct Communication and concurrent Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse, then transferred to concurrent Left Leader of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return from the mission he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Secretariat in Direct Communication and concurrent Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse, then transferred to concurrent Left Leader of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 聰微習弓馬，乃以將用自許。

translations.literal: Cong had slightly practiced bow and horse and then promised himself for general's use.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had dabbled in archery and horsemanship and now fancied himself fit for military command.

sentences.zh: 高祖銳意南討，專訪王肅以軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was keen on the southern campaign and exclusively consulted Wang Su on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was keen on the southern campaign and consulted Wang Su exclusively on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 聰託肅願以偏裨自効，肅言之於高祖，故假聰輔國將軍，統兵二千，與劉藻、傅永、成道益、任莫問俱受肅節度，同援渦陽。

translations.literal: Cong entreated Su, wishing to serve as a flank officer; Su spoke of this to Emperor Xiaowen, so Cong was given acting rank General Who Assists the State, commanding two thousand troops; with Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Cheng Daoyi, and Ren Mokou he all received Su's command and jointly aided Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cong entreated Su, wishing to serve as a flank officer; Su spoke of this to Emperor Xiaowen, so Cong was given acting rank as General Who Assists the State and commanded two thousand troops. With Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Cheng Daoyi, and Ren Mokou he all served under Su's command and jointly relieved Woyang.

sentences.zh: 而聰躁怯少威重，所經淫掠無禮，及與賊交，望風退敗。

translations.literal: But Cong was rash and cowardly, with little awe-inspiring weight; wherever he passed he wantonly plundered without propriety, and when he met the bandits he retreated defeated at the sight of them.
translations.idiomatic: But Cong was rash and cowardly, commanding little respect; wherever he passed he wantonly plundered without restraint, and when he met the bandits he fled at the sight of them.

sentences.zh: 與藻等同囚於懸瓠，高祖恕死，徙平州為民。

translations.literal: With Zao and the others he was imprisoned together at Xuanhu; Emperor Xiaowen spared his life and exiled him to Ping province as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: With Zao and the others he was imprisoned at Xuanhu; Emperor Xiaowen spared his life and exiled him to Ping province as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 行屆瀛州，屬刺史王質獲白兔將獻，託聰為表。

translations.literal: On the journey he reached Ying province; it happened that Inspector Wang Zhi had obtained a white hare to present and entrusted Cong to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey he reached Ying province; it happened that Inspector Wang Zhi had obtained a white hare to present and entrusted Cong to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 高祖見表，顧謂王肅曰：「在下那得復有此才，而令朕不知也？

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen saw the memorial and, turning, said to Wang Su: "How could men below still produce such talent, yet leave Me ignorant of it?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen saw the memorial and, turning, said to Wang Su, "How could men below still produce such talent, yet leave me ignorant of it?

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「比高聰北徙，此文或其所製。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Recently Gao Cong was exiled north; this text is perhaps his composition.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said, "Recently Gao Cong was exiled north; this text is perhaps his composition.

sentences.zh: 」高祖悟曰：「必應然也，何應更有此輩？」

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowen understood and said: "Surely it must be so—how could there be another such?"
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen understood and said, "Surely it must be so—how could there be another such?"

sentences.zh: 世宗初，聰復竊還京師。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign Cong secretly returned to the capital again.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign Cong secretly returned to the capital again.

sentences.zh: 六輔之廢，聰之謀也。

translations.literal: The abolition of the Six Assistants was Cong's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The abolition of the Six Assistants was Cong's stratagem.

sentences.zh: 世宗親政，除給事黃門侍郎，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took personal rule, Cong was appointed Attendant-in-Waiting of the Yellow Gate and given added rank General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took personal rule, Cong was appointed Attendant-in-Waiting of the Yellow Gate and given added rank as General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，黃門如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant Cavalier, his Yellow Gate post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant Cavalier while retaining his Yellow Gate post.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸鄴，還於河內懷界，帝親射矢一里五十餘步。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu visited Ye; returning at the boundary of Henei commandery's Huai district, the emperor personally shot an arrow one li and fifty-odd paces.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Ye, Emperor Xuanwu was returning through the Huai district of Henei when he personally shot an arrow more than a li and fifty paces.

sentences.zh: 侍中高顯等奏：「伏見親御弧矢，臨原弋遠，弦動羽馳，矢鏃所逮，三百五十餘步。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Waiting Gao Xian and others memorialized: "We have observed Your Majesty personally wielding the bow, shooting on the plain at distant targets; when the string moves the feather flies, the arrowhead reaches three hundred fifty-odd paces.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Waiting Gao Xian and others memorialized: "We observe Your Majesty personally drawing the bow, shooting on the plain at distant targets; when the string sounds the feather flies, and the arrowhead reaches more than three hundred fifty paces.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏惟陛下聖武自天，神藝夙茂，巧會騶虞之節，妙盡矍圃之儀。

translations.literal: We your servants reflect that Your Majesty's sacred martial prowess comes from Heaven, divine skill long flourishing, skillfully matching the rhythms of Zouyu, wonderfully exhausting the ceremonies of the hunting park.
translations.idiomatic: We your servants reflect that Your Majesty's sacred martial prowess comes from Heaven, your divine skill long flourishing, skillfully matching the rhythms of Zouyu and wonderfully mastering the ceremonies of the hunting park.

sentences.zh: 威稜攸疊，甝兇懾氣，才猛所振，勁憝弭心，足以肅截九區，赫服八宇矣。

translations.literal: Majesty piled upon majesty—fierce beasts quelled their breath; wherever talent and valor struck, the hard-hearted subdued their hearts—sufficient to awe the nine regions and brilliantly subdue the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Your majesty mounts upon majesty; fierce beasts quell their breath; wherever talent and valor strike, the stubborn bend their hearts—enough to awe the nine regions and subdue the eight directions in splendor.

sentences.zh: 盛事奇迹，必宜表述，請勒銘射宮，永彰聖藝。

translations.literal: Such a grand event and miracle must surely be set forth; we beg to inscribe the shooting hall, forever to manifest sacred skill.
translations.idiomatic: Such a grand event and marvel must surely be proclaimed; we beg that an inscription be carved at the shooting ground to manifest your sacred skill forever.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「此乃弓弧小藝，何足以示後葉，而喉脣近侍苟以為然，亦豈容有異，便可如請。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "This is but a small art of bow and string—how could it suffice to show posterity? Yet the throat-and-lip attendants rashly think it so; could one permit dissent? Let it be as requested.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict said: "This is but a trifling art of bow and string—how could it suffice to instruct posterity? Yet you throat-and-lip attendants rashly agree; could I permit dissent? Proceed as requested.

sentences.zh: 」遂刊銘於射所，聰為之詞。

translations.literal: " Then they carved an inscription at the shooting ground; Cong composed the wording.
translations.idiomatic: " An inscription was then carved at the shooting ground, with Cong composing the text.

sentences.zh: 趙脩嬖幸，聰深朋附。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiu was a favorite; Cong deeply befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu was a court favorite, and Cong became his devoted ally.

sentences.zh: 及詔追贈脩父，聰為碑文，出入同載，觀視碑石。

translations.literal: When an edict posthumously enfeoffed Xiu's father, Cong wrote the epitaph; they rode in and out in the same carriage, viewing the stele.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict posthumously enfeoffed Xiu's father, Cong wrote the epitaph; they rode together in and out of court, inspecting the stone.

sentences.zh: 聰每見脩，迎送盡禮。

translations.literal: Whenever Cong saw Xiu he met and sent him off with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cong saw Xiu he received and sent him off with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 聰又為脩作表，陳當時便宜，教其自安之術，由是迭相親狎。

translations.literal: Cong also drafted memorials for Xiu, setting forth timely expedients and teaching him arts of self-preservation; thereby they became intimately close in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Cong also drafted memorials for Xiu, setting forth timely expedients and teaching him how to secure his position; thereby they grew intimately close.

sentences.zh: 脩死，甄琛、李憑皆被黜落，聰亦深用危慮。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Zhen Chen and Li Ping were both dismissed, and Cong was deeply anxious.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu died, Zhen Chen and Li Ping were both dismissed, and Cong was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 而聰先以疏宗之情，曲事高肇，竟獲自免，肇之力也。

translations.literal: But Cong had earlier through distant-clan ties curried favor with Gao Zhao and ultimately escaped punishment—Zhao's power.
translations.idiomatic: But Cong had earlier, through distant clan ties, curried favor with Gao Zhao and ultimately escaped punishment—thanks to Zhao's power.

sentences.zh: 脩之任勢，聰傾身事之，及脩之死，言必毀惡。

translations.literal: While Xiu held power Cong threw himself into serving him; when Xiu died he spoke only to denigrate him.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiu held power Cong threw himself into serving him; after Xiu's death he spoke only to denigrate him.

sentences.zh: 茹皓之寵，聰又媚附，每相招命，言笑攜撫，公私託仗，無所不至。

translations.literal: When Ru Hao gained favor Cong again fawned upon him; they constantly summoned each other, laughing and clasping in intimacy, entrusting public and private affairs without limit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ru Hao gained favor Cong fawned upon him again; they constantly summoned each other, laughing and clasping in intimacy, entrusting public and private affairs without limit.

sentences.zh: 每稱皓才識明敏，非趙脩之儔。

translations.literal: He often praised Hao's talent and keen discernment, not Zhao Xiu's sort.
translations.idiomatic: He often praised Hao's talent and keen discernment as no match for Zhao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 乃因皓啟請青州鎮下治中公廨，以為私宅，又乞水田數十頃，皆被遂許。

translations.literal: Then through Hao he memorialized requesting the Zhonghe government compound under Qingzhou garrison for a private residence, and also begged several dozen qing of irrigated fields—all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Then through Hao he memorialized requesting the Zhonghe government compound under the Qingzhou garrison as a private residence, and also begged several dozen qing of irrigated fields—all were granted.

sentences.zh: 及皓見戮，聰以為死之晚也。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed Cong thought death had come too late.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was executed Cong thought his death had come too late.

sentences.zh: 其薄於情義，類皆如此。

translations.literal: His thinness in feeling and righteousness were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His want of feeling and loyalty were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 侍中高顯出授護軍，聰轉兼其處，於時顯兄弟疑聰間構而求之。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Waiting Gao Xian went out to take the Protector Army command; Cong transferred to hold his post concurrently; at that time Xian's brothers suspected Cong of intrigue and sought to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: When Attendant-in-Waiting Gao Xian went out to command the Protector Army, Cong transferred to hold his post concurrently; Xian's brothers then suspected Cong of intrigue and sought his removal.

sentences.zh: 聰居兼十餘旬，出入機要，言即真，無遠慮。

translations.literal: Cong held the concurrent post more than ten decadal days, entering and leaving crucial affairs; his words were immediately adopted, without far-reaching thought.
translations.idiomatic: Cong held the concurrent post for more than ten decadal days, entering and leaving crucial affairs; his words were immediately adopted, without far-reaching thought.

sentences.zh: 藉貴因權，耽於聲色，賄納之音，聞於遐邇。

translations.literal: Relying on eminence and exploiting power, addicted to sound and beauty; news of bribe-taking reached far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on eminence and exploiting power, he indulged in music and women; reports of bribe-taking reached far and near.

sentences.zh: 中尉崔亮知肇微恨，遂面陳聰罪，世宗乃出聰為平北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang knew Zhao bore slight resentment and thereupon presented Cong's crimes in person; Emperor Xuanwu then sent Cong out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang knew Zhao bore him slight resentment and thereupon presented Cong's crimes in person; Emperor Xuanwu then sent Cong out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 聰善於去就，知肇嫌之，側身承奉，肇遂待之如舊。

translations.literal: Cong was skilled at coming and going; knowing Zhao resented him he turned his body to serve and fawn; Zhao then treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was skilled at shifting with fortune; knowing Zhao resented him he bent himself to serve and fawn, and Zhao then treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 聰在并州數歲，多不率法，又與太原太守王椿有隙，再為大使、御史舉奏，肇每以宗私相援，事得寢緩。

translations.literal: Cong was several years in Bing province, largely not following law; he also had friction with Taiyuan Prefect Wang Chun; twice envoys and censors impeached him; Zhao each time aided him on clan ties, and matters were allowed to slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Cong spent several years in Bing province, largely ignoring the law; he also clashed with Taiyuan Prefect Wang Chun. Envoys and censors impeached him twice, but Zhao each time shielded him on clan grounds and the cases were allowed to subside.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，拜散騎常侍、平北將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐祚，以其素附高肇，出為幽州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoming ascended, because he had long attached himself to Gao Zhao he was sent out as Inspector of You province, general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming ascended, because he had long been attached to Gao Zhao he was sent out as Inspector of You province, his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋以高肇之黨，與王世義、高綽、李憲、崔楷、蘭氛之為中尉元匡所彈，靈太后並特原之。

translations.literal: Soon as a member of Gao Zhao's faction, together with Wang Shiyi, Gao Chuo, Li Xian, Cui Kai, and Lan Fen he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang; Empress Dowager Ling specially pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as a member of Gao Zhao's faction, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang together with Wang Shiyi, Gao Chuo, Li Xian, Cui Kai, and Lan Fen. Empress Dowager Ling specially pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 聰遂停廢于家，斷絕人事，唯修營園果，以聲色自娛。

translations.literal: Cong was then suspended at home, cutting off human intercourse, only cultivating gardens and orchards, amusing himself with sound and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was then suspended at home, cutting off social contact, cultivating only gardens and orchards and amusing himself with music and women.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜光祿大夫，加安北將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with added rank General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with added rank as General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 聰心望中書令，然後出作青州，願竟不果。

translations.literal: Cong's heart set on Director of the Secretariat, yet afterward was sent out as Inspector of Qing province—the wish ultimately unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had set his heart on Director of the Secretariat, yet was afterward sent out as Inspector of Qing province—the wish was never fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 正光元年夏卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Zhenguang he died, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the first year of Zhenguang he died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 靈太后聞其病，遣主書問之，聰對使者歔欷慟泣。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling heard he was ill and sent a chief clerk to inquire; Cong answered the envoy with sobs and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling heard he was ill and sent a chief clerk to inquire; Cong answered the envoy with sobs and tears.

sentences.zh: 及聞其亡，嗟悼良久，言：「朕既無福，大臣殞喪。

translations.literal: When she heard he had died she sighed and mourned long, saying: "We are without fortune; a great minister has perished.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard of his death she sighed and mourned at length, saying, "We are without fortune; a great minister has perished.

sentences.zh: 且其與朕父南征，契闊戎旅，特可感念。

translations.literal: Moreover he campaigned south with Our Father, sharing hardships on campaign—especially moving to recall.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he campaigned south with our father, sharing hardships on campaign—especially moving to recall.

sentences.zh: 」賵布帛三百匹、冰一車。

translations.literal: " Funeral gifts of three hundred bolts of cloth and silk and one cart of ice.
translations.idiomatic: " She granted funeral gifts of three hundred bolts of cloth and silk and one cart of ice.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、青州刺史，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Qing province, posthumous title Xian (Accomplished).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Qing province, with the posthumous title Xian (Accomplished).

sentences.zh: 聰有妓十餘人，有子無子皆注籍為妾，以悅其情。

translations.literal: Cong had more than ten singing girls; whether they had sons or not he all registered them as concubines to please his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Cong kept more than ten singing girls; whether or not they had borne sons he registered them all as concubines to please himself.

sentences.zh: 及病，不欲他人得之，並令燒指吞炭，出家為尼。

translations.literal: When ill, not wishing others to obtain them, he had them all burn their fingers and swallow charcoal and leave home as nuns.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, not wishing others to have them, he had them all burn their fingers, swallow charcoal, and leave home as nuns.

sentences.zh: 聰所作文筆二十卷，別有集。

translations.literal: Cong's literary compositions in twenty scrolls, with a separate collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Cong left literary compositions in twenty scrolls, with a separate collected works.

sentences.zh: 子長雲，字彥鴻。

translations.literal: His son Changyun, style name Yanhong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Changyun, courtesy name Yanhong.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎、太尉主簿，稍遷輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: On first entering office Secretariat Gentleman and Chief Clerk of the Grand Master of War; gradually promoted to General Who Assists the State and Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first entering office he was made Secretariat Gentleman and Chief Clerk of the Grand Master of War; he was gradually promoted to General Who Assists the State and Palace Cadet.

sentences.zh: 建義初，於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyi he met violent death at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyi he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 長雲弟叔山，字彥甫。

translations.literal: Changyun's younger brother Shushan, style name Yanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Changyun's younger brother was Shushan, courtesy name Yanfu.

sentences.zh: 司徒行參軍，稍遷寧朔將軍、越騎校尉。

translations.literal: Runner Aide to the Minister of the Masses; gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of Upright Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was Runner Aide to the Minister of the Masses and was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of Upright Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：甄琛以學尚刀筆，早樹聲名，受遇三朝，終至崇重。

translations.literal: The chronicler says: Zhen Chen, by learning and skill in drafting, early built a reputation, was favored through three reigns, and in the end reached high honor.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler says: Zhen Chen, through learning and skill in drafting, early built a reputation, was favored through three reigns, and in the end reached high honor.

sentences.zh: 高聰才尚見知，名位顯著。

translations.literal: Gao Cong's talent was valued and he was known; name and position were eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cong's talent was recognized and his name and position were eminent.

sentences.zh: 而異軌同奔，咸經於危覆之轍，惜乎！

translations.literal: Yet by different tracks they ran together, all passing through tracks of danger and ruin—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet by different paths they ran alike, all passing through tracks of ruin—alas!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 世有其民 冊府卷四九三

translations.literal: "Each age has its people" — Cefu guangji, juan 493
translations.idiomatic: Note on "each age has its people" (世有其民): Cefu guangji, juan 493

sentences.zh: 〈五八九四頁〉
「有」作「育」，據下文作「育」是。

translations.literal: "You" (有) is written as "yu" (育); according to the following text "yu" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The character you (有, "have") appears as yu (育, "nurture"); the following passage shows yu is correct.

sentences.zh: 太平中 按魏無「太平」年號，下云「世宗崩」，「太平」當是「永平」之訛。

translations.literal: "In the Taiping era" — Note: Wei has no Taiping reign title; below it says "Emperor Xuanwu died"; "Taiping" must be an error for "Yongping."
translations.idiomatic: "In the Taiping era": Northern Wei has no Taiping reign title; the text below mentions Emperor Xuanwu's death, so Taiping must be a scribal error for Yongping.

sentences.zh: 召楷兼長史 諸本「楷」下衍「不」字，今據北史卷四０甄琛附甄楷傳、冊府卷七二一

translations.literal: "Summoned Kai as acting Chief Administrator" — Various editions have a superfluous "bu" under "Kai"; now per Bei shi juan 40 Zhen Chen fu Zhen Kai zhuan and Cefu juan 721
translations.idiomatic: "Summoned Kai as acting Chief Administrator": various editions insert a superfluous bu after Kai; emended per Bei shi 40 (Zhen Kai biography) and Cefu guangji juan 721

sentences.zh: 〈八五八四頁〉
刪。

translations.literal: deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The superfluous character is deleted.

sentences.zh: 及刺史元固 諸本「固」作「冏」，百衲本作「囧」，也即「冏」字，冊府卷七二一

translations.literal: "When Inspector Yuan Gu" — Various editions read "gu" as "jiong"; the Baipu edition reads "jiong" (variant for jiong), Cefu juan 721
translations.idiomatic: "When Inspector Yuan Gu": various editions read Gu (固) as Jiong (冏); the Baipu edition writes 囧, a variant of Jiong; Cefu guangji juan 721

sentences.zh: 〈八五八五頁〉
作「固」。

translations.literal: reads "gu."
translations.idiomatic: Cefu reads Gu (固).

sentences.zh: 北史卷四０大德本也作「固」，百衲本據殿本修作「冏」。

translations.literal: Bei shi juan 40 Dade edition also reads "gu"; the Baipu edition revised per the Dian edition to "jiong."
translations.idiomatic: Bei shi 40 (Dade edition) also reads Gu; the Baipu edition revised to Jiong following the Dian edition.

sentences.zh: 按卷五八楊播附楊津傳見定州刺史元固。

translations.literal: According to juan 58 Yang Bo fu Yang Jin zhuan, Ding Inspector Yuan Gu appears.
translations.idiomatic: According to Wei shu 58 (Yang Jin biography under Yang Bo), Inspector of Ding Yuan Gu appears.

sentences.zh: 墓誌集釋有元固墓誌

translations.literal: Muzhi jishi has Yuan Gu epitaph
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi jishi includes Yuan Gu's epitaph

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一二０〉

translations.literal: (plate 120)
translations.idiomatic: (plate 120)

sentences.zh: ，也說他曾官「定州刺史」。

translations.literal: , which also says he once held office as "Inspector of Ding province."
translations.idiomatic: , which also records that he once served as Inspector of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 這裏「冏」乃「固」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Here "jiong" is an error for "gu"; emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Here Jiong (冏) is a scribal error for Gu (固); the text is emended accordingly.
